title.narrative: Output 1.1. Increased institutional capacity of employer and business membership organizations (EBMOs)

description.narrative:
In 2022/23,Viet Nam Chamber of Commerce and Industry (VCCI) conducted advocacy activities in the areas of employment policy, labour administration, social security, skills development and ease and cost of doing business. Based on a survey of 1,000 members in 17 provinces on business resilience, VCCI submitted policy recommendations on skills development, social security and active labour market policies in December 2022 to the Ministry of Labour, Invalids and Social Affairs. VCCI communicated its position to the public through website, presentations, and social media channels. Also in 2022, the Chamber published a Provincial Competitiveness Index Report (PCI) based on a survey of 12,000 enterprises which assessed the quality of governance and business environment. The PCI informed state agencies reform of administrative procedures and improving business environments. Furthermore, VCCI developed VIB Online to help businesses better understand legislation and gather their views. Information gathered through VIB Online enabled VCCI to provide inputs on 185 draft bills between January 2022 to June 2023.
In 2023, VCCI conducted an Enterprise Health Survey to support recovery and sustainable development of the business community and a survey on business participation in global value chains reaching 500 enterprises. Additionally, VCCI engaged in advocacy on the social security system by submitting recommendations on the policy development process, including the consultation and the participation of VCCI in the management of the social security fund, to the government in September 2023.
To sustain its newly acquired policy advocacy capacity, VCCI reinvigorated the functions of the Policy Advisory Committee to support the secretariat in VCCI’s policy advocacy by contributing insights to position papers, which had been inactive during the COVID crisis and now convenes every quarter. The ILO supported VCCI in conducting a labour survey on business resilience and recovery in the post-pandemic period by technically contributing to the design and administration of the survey and developing policy recommendations so that VCCI can produce similar evidence-based policy recommendations in the future. The ILO built the organizational capacity of VCCI to use data as a strategic asset by providing Qualtrics (cloud-based software data platform) training twice (July-August 2022 and May 2023). VCCI staff learned how to build a survey, interpret survey results and export data, create dynamic visualizations and reports, customize survey reports, and create a dashboard. The ILO also conducted training workshops on strategic advocacy and effective influencing, communication skills for advocacy (writing policy position papers, news articles, press releases), and digital advocacy through social media in 2023.
The ILO supported VCCI to develop policy recommendations on the social security system in Viet Nam by offering on-the-job training for VCCI staff to ensure sustained institutional expertise and skills are available internally to advance VCCI’s policy agenda. ITC-ILO also offered a regional training on “Governance of Social Security System for Employers” where VCCI staff skills and knowledge on the policy development process related to social security in 2023.
The ILO supported the setting of indicators for the PCI Report to give more weight to the role of the Provincial People’s Committees in industrial relations and labour dispute resolution. For effective engagement in policy advocacy, ILO also provided technical support in strengthening the existing VCCI Policy Advisory Committee to add experts on labour laws and industrial relations.
